title: pvWritePOBJWriter
body:
## pvWritePOBJWriter

Explicit-export writer for Wavefront OBJ (.obj), a plain-text surface format read by almost every 3-D modelling, rendering and visualization tool. It writes the points, lines, triangles and polygons of polygonal data plus point normals and texture coordinates when present; solution fields are not stored. TextureFileName additionally writes a material (.mtl) file that refers to an existing texture image. Publication uses the geometry contract: the file is read back and the triangulated surface is compared, accepting loss of fields, point identity, interior cells and structure. Use pvWritePSTLWriter for triangle-only CAD or 3-D printing exchange, and VTK XML writers when fields matter.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Scalar and vector fields (pressure, velocity, ...) are lost; export a VTK XML format when the receiver needs them.
- TextureFileName is written into the .mtl as given and the image is not copied into the output folder; use a path that still resolves where the OBJ will be opened.
- An earlier catalogue run (verification/2026-09-16-catalogue-expansion.json, writerQualification) passed only on a small serial fixture with a tolerance of 1e-6 and the other options at their defaults; no current native acceptance check is recorded, so verify the export on representative data.

Native constructor: `POBJWriter`. Identity: `writers/POBJWriter`. Role: `writer`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Connect upstream object to `Input` | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellDataArrays` | Select the cell data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ChooseArraysToWrite` | Explicitly choose which arrays to write. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `EdgeDataArrays` | Select the edge data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FieldDataArrays` | Select the field data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `NumberOfIORanks` | In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out. | `{"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |
| `PointDataArrays` | Select the point data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `RankAssignmentMode` | In MPI runs where NumberOfIORanks is greater than 1 and less than the number of ranks, chooses how ranks are grouped to send data to the writing ranks. Contiguous forms consecutive groups (16 ranks, 3 writers: 0-5, 6-10, 11-15, written by ranks 0, 6 and 11); RoundRobin interleaves them (0, 3, ..., 15; 1, 4, ..., 13; 2, 5, ..., 14, written by 0, 1 and 2). Schemaxis runs explicit exports serially, so this has no effect on the file. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Contiguous","RoundRobin"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Contiguous"` |
| `RowDataArrays` | Select the row data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `TextureFileName` | Optional. The name of the texture map file to be written into the mtl file. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `VertexDataArrays` | Select the vertex data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Output publication contract:

```json
{
  "comparison": "geometry",
  "extensions": [
    "obj"
  ],
  "filenames": "managed output directory",
  "losses": [
    "fields",
    "point-identity",
    "interior-cells",
    "structure"
  ],
  "qualification": "requires fixture",
  "time": "one scheduled state"
}
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "explicit exports with semantic readback",
  "outputPorts": 0,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `scenes[].exports`; writers cannot be graph nodes. The main data input is `node`; non-data ports go in `resources`.

```json
{
  "id": "exportResult",
  "node": "DATA_NODE",
  "writer": "pvWritePOBJWriter",
  "acceptLosses": [
    "fields",
    "point-identity",
    "interior-cells",
    "structure"
  ]
}
```
